subject: Is your eval layer as strong as your engagement stat?
text:
Hi [NAME],

From the research I've done, [COMPANY]'s agent teams close care gaps, verify coverage, and book appointments in one coordinated workflow.

The agentic AI infrastructure is strong. The gap most teams in this position hit is the human review layer, a systematic way to catch agent output errors before they reach members, and an audit trail that satisfies payer compliance requirements.

We work with healthcare and enterprise AI teams on that layer, including Appfolio and Synthesia on text and document workflows.

Without it:

• 
Agent failures compound silently before member impact.

• 
Payer audits surface gaps in model output traceability.

Worth 20 minutes this week to show what that setup looks like?

subject: The data-layer question behind VLAs and world models
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've been speaking to some members of the [COMPANY] team, so thought
it would be worth speaking to you too.

At Encord, we sit underneath the physical-AI stack as the data layer
(collection, curation, multimodal annotation, eval) for teams training VLA
models, world models, and embodied agents.

If you're scanning frontier bets for [COMPANY]'s 3-5 year roadmap, the
question worth pressure-testing is: how will ST capture, curate, and align

will demand? Most groups discover the data layer is the rate-limiter on
capability, not the model side.

Happy to share what we're seeing across frontier-research groups (Toyota
Research, Forterra, and others) without a pitch.
